title: OpenAI Gives Free ChatGPT Users Unlimited Text Chats and Upgrades Default Model
excerpt: Free and Go users get GPT-5.6 Luna as their default model with no text-based rate limits, while Plus and Pro users receive an upgraded GPT-5.6 Sol with fewer factual errors.
body:
• Free and Go ChatGPT users will get unlimited text chats starting next week, with GPT-5.6 Luna replacing GPT-5.5 Instant as the default model.
  • Plus and Pro users get an upgraded GPT-5.6 Sol that OpenAI says makes 68% fewer factual errors than GPT-5.5 Instant, with a new slider to control reasoning depth.
  • Limits on file uploads, images, and other tools still apply for free users; only text chats are unlimited.
  • A new Think button will let free users access deeper reasoning for harder questions.

OpenAI announced Thursday that it is removing text-based rate limits for free ChatGPT users and upgrading their default model to GPT-5.6 Luna, marking one of the most significant expansions of its free tier since the chatbot's launch.

What's Changing for Free Users

Starting next week, Free and Go tier ChatGPT users will be able to have unlimited text conversations with no daily or weekly caps. The default model switches from GPT-5.5 Instant to GPT-5.6 Luna, a newer and more capable model from OpenAI's latest generation, according to MacRumors.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=0PpIELi66xw

The change applies only to text-based chats. Limits will continue to apply for file uploads, image generation, and other ChatGPT tools. OpenAI is also adding a "Think" button that will let free users activate deeper reasoning for harder questions.

Paid Users Get a Smarter Sol

For Plus and Pro subscribers, OpenAI rolled out an updated version of GPT-5.6 Sol on Thursday. The company said the updated model is "more reliable with facts" and gives "more focused answers," reducing factual errors by 68% compared to GPT-5.5 Instant, according to OpenAI's announcement.

A new slider lets users control how much thought ChatGPT puts into each response, allowing them to balance speed against depth. OpenAI also said Sol will avoid unnecessary formatting and offer "a helpful correction when simply agreeing wouldn't be useful" — an apparent nod to longstanding complaints about AI sycophancy.

The Sol improvements specifically target accuracy on answers that depend on dates, numbers, sources, rules, or assumptions. The update applies to ChatGPT's chat interface only; the Work and Codex versions remain unchanged.

Context: OpenAI's Free Tier Strategy

The move reflects OpenAI's evolving approach to competition. After defaulting free users to the cheaper GPT-5.2 Instant model in December 2025 — a cost-cutting measure — the company is now reversing course by giving them access to a GPT-5.6 family model at no cost.

The shift comes as OpenAI faces intensifying competition from Google's Gemini and Anthropic's Claude, both of which have expanded their free offerings. OpenAI recently gave ChatGPT Plus subscriptions free to college students in a separate move to grow its user base.

The company has also been easing usage restrictions on GPT-5.6 for paid users. Thibault Sottiaux, OpenAI's head of core products, recently announced the removal of 5-hour usage windows for Plus, Business, and Pro users, and the company cut Luna's API price by 80% in late July, according to Android Authority.

What This Means for Users

For the more than 100 million weekly ChatGPT users, the update means the free product becomes substantially more capable. Luna sits in the GPT-5.6 family alongside the more expensive Sol and mid-tier Terra models, representing a significant step up from the previous free-tier model.

The 68% reduction in factual errors for Sol is particularly notable for professionals who rely on ChatGPT for research, coding, or analysis — tasks where accuracy matters more than conversational fluency.

What's Next

GPT-5.6 Luna becomes the default for Free and Go users this week, with the unlimited text chats and Think button rolling out next week. OpenAI has also teased Astra, an unreleased model designed for complex, long-running tasks, suggesting the pace of model releases shows no signs of slowing.
